newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks slip to lower close in active trade.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks slip to lower close in active trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks slipped to a moderately lower close on Friday on profit-taking in the market's defensive sectors, and the index was likely to continue to trend weaker on regional currency worries, brokers said.

"There is still lots of momentum in the market, but there is also a good deal of caution from institutions who are worried about the fallout from Thailand," said one analyst with a large European brokerage.
The Hang Seng Index closed 51.11 points, or 0.33 percent, lower at 15,658.12. Trading activity picking up in the afternoon an the index touched a low of 15,631.93.
Turnover rose to a robust HK$18.96 billion, slightly higher than Thursday's HK$18.33 billion.
Most Asian markets, including Hong Kong, have come under pressure, derived in part from concerns over the near-term stability of regional currencies.
Hong Kong's monetary authority said on Friday that it is not worried about a speculative attack on the Hong Kong dollar.
Trading in the Hong Kong dollar settled down on Friday but tension lingered after a sharp upward spike in currency forwards on Thursday created expectations of a speculative attack, traders said.
Brokers said there's no definable trend in the market.
"We saw choppy intra-day trading," said one trader at a U.S. brokerage. "The forecast rally in the property investors didn't materialise."
The defensive utility sector, which had been bid up to record levels recently, led the market down, followed at a distance by banks, while the property sector tended higher.
Hongkong Electric closed HK$0.60 down at HK$31.90 and HK and China Gas shed HK$0.55 to HK$15.95, although both shares were only moderately traded.

China Light lost HK$0.20 to HK$44.50. The company reported an 18 percent rise in turnover in the nine months ended June 30 from the year-earlier period, derived chiefly from a 5.3 percent rise in electricity sales
HSBC and subsidiary Hang Seng Bank slumped HK$1.00 each to HK$262.00 and HK$114.00 respectively. Cheung Kong edged up HK$0.50 to HK$75.55.
CCT Telecom was the most active issue, rising HK$0.32 to HK$1.35 after announcing plans to invest in China's telecommunications industry.
Hopewell lost HK$0.125 to HK$4.725 after news the company's Thai project needed a financing solution by end-July.
